replacement.title: All-Unit Toilet Drain Alignment
replacement.definition: Position the bathrooms and toilets across the new dwellings relative to the existing waste pipes so feasible connections are maintained, independently of the unit 3-specific routing dispute.

patches.decision_note: Messages 1 and 41 establish a general drain-alignment constraint for the new bathrooms, while later messages 44–48 describe a separate unit 3-specific routing trajectory.

value_updates.bathroom_placement_constraint: Account for the two shown toilet waste pipes when positioning the new bathrooms.

patches.decision_note: The source concerns the new bathrooms generally and does not support limiting the initial scope to unit 3.
The plural bathroom-placement constraint applies across the subdivision rather than specifically to the unit 3 drain route.
The client asks for toilet positions generally to be updated according to existing drains; unit 3 is not the sole target.
The source reports successful dimensional adjustment but does not identify unit 1 or its en-suite bathroom unambiguously.
Sending the plan is a hand-off update and does not explicitly claim that the floor-plan deliverable is implemented or complete.
The freelancer says only that the dimension is being added; this reports ongoing activity rather than a completed target-specific implementation claim.
Review the omitted image context to determine whether the dimensional-fit result belongs to another specific bathroom Requirement after deletion from the unit 1 en-suite lifecycle.
Attachment context is needed to determine whether message 30 changes the unit 3 counter location and whether the short approval in message 33 accepts that specific proposal.
Message 50 may contain a missed change to common entrance-hall allocation, but its verbatim source text is not supplied here for a safe ADD_EVENT patch.
The marked-image context is required to identify which unit 1 bathroom is expanded to the turquoise boundary and whether a separate common-bathroom geometry Requirement is missing.
Message 83 appears to introduce an additional dimension annotation, but its verbatim text is unavailable in the audit payload and must be inspected before adding the Event.
Confirm whether message 94 unambiguously accepts retaining the existing arrangement; message 96 indicates that the freelancer still considered the swap decision unresolved.
The missing image marker prevents reliable identification of the toilet and therefore prevents safe routing to a unit-specific drain-alignment Requirement.
